text: You already learned tagging for cost allocation, and budgets plus anomaly detection, in the FinOps course earlier in this path. None of that mechanism changes for AI infrastructure. What changes is how urgently it matters, because of everything this chapter has covered about how fast GPU spend moves.

Apply the same taxonomy to the resources a training job actually touches - the GPU instance or node pool, the storage holding datasets and checkpoints, any managed training service in use. Team, project, environment, same as always, plus one tag that matters more here than anywhere else: job-type, separating training from inference, because the two have such different right-sizing profiles that a single undifferentiated GPU number hides which one actually moved. Enforce it the same way - Azure Policy denying an untagged GPU resource, or an AWS tag policy requiring team and project on GPU instance types.

An untagged resource sits in the same uncounted bucket regardless of what it is - but an untagged GPU resource sits there at an order of magnitude higher cost per hour than an untagged CPU VM. The mechanism for fixing it hasn't changed since the FinOps course. The cost of skipping it has gotten much worse.

That same logic argues for a dedicated GPU budget rather than folding GPU spend into one subscription-wide number. A general budget set at eighty and a hundred percent can take days to trip on GPU overspend because it's diluted inside everything else. A budget scoped specifically to GPU-tagged spend, with tighter thresholds and ideally a forecasted threshold that fires before the month even ends, catches the same dollar amount far earlier - and anomaly detection scoped the same way catches a forgotten notebook or a stuck job within hours, not at the next scheduled review.

Put the whole chapter together: understanding why GPU spend runs away so fast is why spot plus checkpointing and disciplined training-versus-inference right-sizing matter so much here, and tagging every job plus a dedicated GPU budget is what makes all of it visible before it becomes a surprise. That's a real FinOps practice for AI infrastructure, not four separate tips. Next chapter turns to scaling and reliability - capacity planning, multi-region strategy, and SLOs for inference.
